response.internal_assessment: The $0.12 price point changes everything I was still holding in reserve. At $0.18 I could still tell myself that car ownership had a cost floor that robotaxis could not breach for most households — the insurance, the parking, the convenience of having the vehicle in your driveway at 6 AM. At $0.12 with 8-minute wait times and residential coverage, that argument is gone. The person who lives in Millfield's east side neighborhoods and drove 12 miles to work every day is now looking at $1.44 each way — less than a gallon of gas, with no parking problem and no insurance bill. The delivery partnership means the errand-runner use case is captured too. The last geographic argument I had — that people in residential areas would still need their own cars because RoboRide did not serve them — is dead this tick. Rick's assessment was supposed to give me two weeks of breathing room to make the consolidation decision carefully. I am not throwing out his work, but I am compressing the timeline. I cannot wait another ten days to formally initiate location reduction. The sector index is at 79 and falling. Tamika Jefferson may be making a move — that word-of-mouth from Betty or someone in the network means one of my better salespeople is already looking for the exit. Angela and Rick are both stressed per the inbox. This is the month I have to call the consolidation, not the month I finish planning it.
response.inbox_interpretation: RoboRide's residential expansion is the critical datum — it confirms the sales volume model is irretrievably compromised for the mass-market segment. The 7% regular usage number is still small but the direction is unambiguous and accelerating. The sector index at 79 means I have already lost roughly one in five revenue dollars and the floor has not arrived yet. Rick Tanner being 'stressed' in the social signal likely means he has completed or nearly completed the assessment and the numbers are worse than the framework he brought me. Tamika's potential departure is a talent-flight early warning — salespeople read market conditions in their commissions before I read them in reports. The mood around Angela is also tense, which may mean the vulnerability map surfaced something the team is not yet ready to act on. I need to move before I lose more of the human infrastructure that makes a restructured business viable.

chosen_actions.description: Formally accelerate the consolidation timeline. Call Rick Tanner today and inform him that the RoboRide residential expansion requires advancing the assessment conclusion from two weeks to 72 hours. I am not asking for a perfect document — I am asking for his current best read on which of the four locations has the weakest service-lane foundation and which has the strongest. The decision I am making is to close one sales floor location — the lowest-performing on service lane throughput and lease flexibility — by end of Q2. This is not a contingency plan. I am committing to it now and asking Rick to confirm which location the data supports. The service technicians at the closed location will be offered transfers to the surviving locations before any external hiring happens. Sales floor staff at the closed location will be informed within one week and processed through Angela's transition program.

resources.detail: Accelerated consolidation directive — close one sales floor location by end of Q2 based on Rick's asset map; service technicians given transfer priority; sales staff transitioned through Angela's program

chosen_actions.reasoning: At $0.12/mile with residential coverage, every month I continue operating a fourth sales floor is a month I am paying lease, utilities, floor staff, and management overhead on a unit that will not recover. The service lane at that location can be absorbed by the other three. The financial relief from closing one location — estimated at roughly $8,000/month in reduced fixed overhead net of transition costs — extends my runway and concentrates resources in the service-lane core that actually has a future. Waiting for the perfect data is the 2008 mistake in reverse: moving too slowly because the information is not complete.

chosen_actions.description: Send a brief, professional note to Angela Wright acknowledging that the RoboRide residential expansion changes the consolidation timeline and that she should expect formal notification within 72 hours of which location is closing and how many positions are affected. Ask her to confirm that the transition program pipeline — the Maria Santos grant connection, the First Community Bank small-dollar loans, the community college enrollment pathway — is active and that case managers are in place. Tell her I want every affected employee contacted within 48 hours of announcement, not 72. Tell her the service tech transfer list is her first coordination priority before we go to any external hire.

resources.detail: Advance notice to HR Director of accelerated consolidation timeline; pipeline readiness check; service tech transfer prioritization directive

chosen_actions.reasoning: Angela's retention bonus and her role as transition architect only pays off if she has lead time. If I call the consolidation formally without giving her advance notice, I waste the infrastructure I spent $12,000 to build. One note today means the transition program is ready to execute the moment the announcement drops.

chosen_actions.description: Reach out to Tamika Jefferson directly — not through a manager, not through email — and ask her to come in for a 20-minute conversation this week. Do not frame it as a performance check. Frame it honestly: I have heard there may be something she is considering and I want to hear from her directly before she makes any decision. If she is thinking about leaving, I want to know if there is a role in a restructured organization that would keep her. The service advisor and fleet-account relationship role I have been building toward in the service-lane model needs someone who can sell relationships, not just units. If Tamika is that person and she knows it, I want her to hear that from me before she hears it from anyone else.

resources.detail: Retention conversation with Tamika Jefferson — direct outreach to understand her intentions and potentially reframe her role toward the service-lane model

chosen_actions.reasoning: Talent-flight is a leading indicator. The word-of-mouth about Tamika making a move, combined with the tense mood around the team, tells me she is already reading the writing on the wall. If she leaves, she takes institutional knowledge, customer relationships, and a signal to the rest of the floor that the smart people are walking. A 20-minute conversation costs me nothing. Losing her without trying costs me more than I can measure right now.

response.inner_monologue: My father ran one lot. I told myself for twenty years that four locations meant I had built something bigger than what he handed me. Today I am calling Rick to tell him we are closing one of them and I feel something closer to relief than grief, which tells me I have already done the grieving. The question is not whether the business survives in its current shape — it does not — the question is whether what survives is worth the name we put on it. I think it is. But I have to stop protecting the shape of it and start protecting the core.
